To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lymphocyte membrane contains a collagen‐binding component which mediates motility of the lymphocyte when the cell contacts a two‐dimensional substratum‐bound ligand.

the motile behavior of freshly isolated human T lymphocytes is induced by collagen‐type I and that this effect is mediated by the collagen‐binding receptor(s) present in the lymphocyte plasma membranes.
the lymphocyte surface contains collagen‐binding sites which are responsible for the motile behavior of lymphocytes in the presence of gelatin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the collagen receptor on T lymphocyte membrane may be involved in the control of lymphocytic motility.
the role of collagen in lymphocyte migration.
the role of collagen receptors in lymphocyte motility and the possible involvement of the collagen receptor in the control of lymphocytic immune responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lymphocyte motility‐promoting effect of collagen/gelatin is mediated by a collagen‐binding component of the lymphocyte plasma membranes.
collagen/gelatin is a unique ligand for the induction of lymphocyte motile behavior.
the lymphocyte collagen receptor is a 130‐kDa molecule with a 55‐kD subunit which may represent a collagen‐binding component of plasma fibronectins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the collagen receptor on lymphocytes is a 55‐kD molecule which may be identical to the 55‐kDalton subunit of fibronectin.
the collagen‐binding component on the lymphocyte plasma membranes is a fibronectin receptor.
lymphocyte motility is controlled by the extracellular matrix via the collagen receptor on lymphocyte surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
collagen‐binding receptors on the surface of T lymphocytes are involved in the regulation of lymphocyte motile behavior.
lymphocytes can be induced to move by the presence of collagen and gelatin in a manner that is not mediated through the classical fibronectin receptor.
the collagen‐binding plasma membrane receptors on lymphocytes may be involved in the control of locomotor activity of these cells.
